ov: About 950 species of spiny, globe-shaped echinoderms living on the seabed of every ocean. They crawl slowly on tube feet and mostly graze on algae.

why.dg: Their sharp spines protect them, and in some species the spines are venomous.
why.et: Its roe is prized, especially in Japan, where uni sells for up to ¥40,000 a kilogram.

rg: All oceans, from the tidal zone to the deep sea.
df: Mainly algae; also slow-moving or fixed animals such as sponges.
fx: Left unchecked by predators such as sea otters, urchins can strip the seabed into “urchin barrens”.
